fd7628aa10.q: What is the optimal carbohydrate-to-fructose ratio for endurance athletes consuming more than 60 grams of carbs per hour?
fd7628aa10.a: Once you start fueling with more than 60 grams of carbs per hour, the ratio of glucose and fructose becomes very important because you have transporters in your intestine that can only move over so many glucose molecules per hour, traditionally thought to be 60 grams per hour. CarbsFuel chose a two-to-one ratio, meaning for every two glucose molecules, there is one fructose molecule.

fd7628aa10.rq: The faster you push, the quicker you burn through that fuel tank, so to speak. So what that means is that over time, and this gets to what you were asking earlier, this will begin to decline over time.

f4ffc4de5c.q: How long can endurance athletes typically perform without fueling before glycogen depletion becomes a limiting factor?
f4ffc4de5c.a: For most performances under 90 minutes to 120 minutes, roughly an hour and a half to two hours, athletes have enough glycogen on board to keep them fueled for their event. However, once glycogen stores start dropping significantly, there is a slow steady decline in performance and athletes cannot push as hard as they could earlier in the event.

9eccb67f27.q: What are the physiological symptoms of bonking or glycogen depletion during endurance exercise?
9eccb67f27.a: Bonking occurs when blood sugar begins to drop because liver glycogen stores can no longer maintain resting glucose levels. Symptoms include feeling very poor, becoming hypoglycemic, getting lightheaded, shaking, and being unable to maintain pace—athletes may have to walk or slow to a crawl because muscles are trying to pull as much glucose as possible while the brain also competes for limited glucose.

7c26f3b236.q: Why does CarbsFuel's 50-gram energy gel cost approximately two dollars compared to three to five dollars per gel packet from competitors?
7c26f3b236.a: CarbsFuel achieves a significantly lower price by using a simpler formulation with no gelling agents and no preservatives, which reduces complexity and cost. By removing unnecessary additives that competitors use, they can offer 50 grams of carbohydrates for roughly two dollars instead of the typical three to five dollars per packet that would require consuming four to six packets per hour at a cost of 20 dollars or more per hour of training.

8fb2fed20a.q: How did different types of maltodextrin affect the texture and stability of CarbsFuel's gel formulation during product development?
8fb2fed20a.a: Aaron discovered that certain maltodextrins, after being heated and cooled, form a gel network that becomes progressively stiffer over time and can eventually become solid, depending on the chain length of glucose molecules and the acidity of the product. This discovery led him to carefully select the correct maltodextrin types to achieve the desired thin, nearly liquid-like gel texture rather than the thick paste-like consistency of traditional gels.
